ns2:section.sectionText: Online & Continuing Education (OCE) restrictions and assessments apply, see http://www.oce.illinois.edu. Flavor Chemistry is a graduate level course that will involve the discussion/demonstration of the chemistry, manufacture/delivery and analysis (sensory/instrumental) of food flavor. The course will cover: principles of food flavor chemistry with emphasis placed on some well-understood flavor systems; techniques/methods used for the manufacture/delivery of food flavorings; modern techniques of analysis/chemical evaluation of food flavor systems; accepted techniques for the sensory evaluation of food flavor systems; approaches for combined sensory-analytical evaluation of food flavor systems and new and emerging areas of flavor research. This class will not meet on September 10 and November 26. The course will be taught via Collaborate v.12 and Compass 2G. Students will need a a web cam, working external microphone/speakers or headset with microphone and reliable high-speed Internet. Access to scanner capable of producing .pdf files required for exam. This section has one or more proctored exams, which may carry additional fees. Proctoring options include fee-based ProctorU and approved proctoring centers, and testing facilities located at the Online & Continuing Education offices on the Urbana-Champaign campus, which carry no fees. For ProctorU technical specifications and additional information visit: http://www.ao.uiuc.edu/support/source/student_services/proctoru_tech.html.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to MS: FSHN (Online) -UIUC, MS:FSci &Hmn Nutrition -UIUC, or NDEG:Grad Nondegree-CE-UIUC.
